Write it yourself or have your provisioning write it, never derive it from a conversation. Serving several people means starting several servers.

environmentVariables.description: A local directory for the bytes. Needs no bucket and no IAM user. Set this OR the S3_* block: with neither, the server refuses to start rather than falling back to memory, which would work in a demo and lose the first real file.

environmentVariables.name: S3_ENDPOINT
environmentVariables.description: An S3-compatible endpoint, for example https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com. Setting it makes S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY required.

environmentVariables.name: S3_BUCKET
environmentVariables.description: The bucket. It must be private: this library decides who may be GIVEN a URL and has no say in who the object store will answer. `npx -p @filelayer/core filelayer doctor` reports whether yours serves unauthenticated reads.

environmentVariables.name: S3_REGION
environmentVariables.description: Region, or `auto` for Cloudflare R2.

environmentVariables.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
environmentVariables.description: Access key id for the bucket.

environmentVariables.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
environmentVariables.description: Secret access key for the bucket.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_AGENT_LABEL
environmentVariables.description: How this agent names itself in the audit trail, recorded on every event these tools produce. It is what lets the chain separate "the partner opened this document" from "the partner's assistant opened this document".

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE
environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register delete_file. Off by default because deleting is not recoverable and an agent that misreads a sentence deletes the wrong thing silently.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_EXPOSE_AUDIT
environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register file_audit. Off by default because the trail is an organisation's whole history and a tool that returns it copies every file name, actor and denial into the model's context. Reading it is itself audited since 0.27.0, which was the previous reason; the default did not move.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_RETURN_BYTES
environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register read_file. Off by default because a document returned by a tool is a document copied into a model's context; file_info plus a share link is usually what was actually needed.

environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_BASE_URL
environmentVariables.description: The base of the share URLs this instance mints. Without it, share links come back without a URL.

servers.name: io.github.iris-eval/mcp-server
servers.title: Iris
servers.description: Stop shipping agents on vibes. Score every agent output for quality, safety, and cost.

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_API_KEY
environmentVariables.description: API key for HTTP authentication. Required to bind the HTTP transport or the dashboard beyond loopback (0.0.0.0, a LAN address, a container): without it the server refuses to start

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_API_KEY_FILE
environmentVariables.description: Path to a file whose trimmed contents are the API key (the secret-file pattern Docker and Kubernetes mount). Set this or IRIS_API_KEY, not both; further keys and rotation are security.apiKeys in config.json

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED
environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to run a non-loopback bind with NO API key on purpose (lifts the startup refusal; the network is then your boundary)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DB_PATH
environmentVariables.description: SQLite database path

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_SQLITE_DRIVER
environmentVariables.description: Which SQLite driver holds the database: native (better-sqlite3, the default) or node (Node's built-in node:sqlite, Node 22.13+). Unset: native, falling back to node when the native module cannot load

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_SEARCH_BUDGET_MS
environmentVariables.description: How long one trace search may read before it answers with the matches found so far, in milliseconds (50-60000, default 1000)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_SEARCH_INDEX
environmentVariables.description: on (default) or off. off keeps no full-text index of the traces: writes are cheaper, and a search reads the traces within its time budget

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LOG_LEVEL
environmentVariables.description: Log level: debug, info, warn, error

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_HOME
environmentVariables.description: Directory for the database, custom rules and preferences (default ~/.iris)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
environmentVariables.description: Enables evaluate_with_llm_judge and verify_citations with an Anthropic model. Optional: the deterministic rules never need a key

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OPENAI_API_KEY
environmentVariables.description: Enables evaluate_with_llm_judge and verify_citations with an OpenAI model. Optional: the deterministic rules never need a key

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_MAX_COST_USD_PER_EVAL
environmentVariables.description: Hard cap on the worst-case cost of one judge or citation call (default 0.25)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_MODEL
environmentVariables.description: A priced judge model; answers_the_ask then asks it on every evaluation with input, sending that input and output to the model's provider, and gates on its verdict (off by default)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD
environmentVariables.description: What the relevance judge may spend per UTC day, per tenant, in USD (default 1); past it answers_the_ask reads the ask lexically

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_MAX_CALLS_PER_REQUEST
environmentVariables.description: Relevance judge calls one request may make (default 20)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_REDACT
environmentVariables.description: on (default) replaces the PII and credentials no_pii flags before the relevance judge sends input and output to its provider; off sends them as they are

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_ALLOW_FETCH
environmentVariables.description: Let verify_citations fetch URLs (off by default)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD
environmentVariables.description: Start the dashboard alongside the server (same as --dashboard)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD_PORT
environmentVariables.description: Dashboard port (default 6920); IRIS_PORT is the MCP HTTP transport port (default 3000)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_PORT
environmentVariables.description: MCP HTTP transport port (default 3000); only used with --transport http

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OTEL_ENDPOINT
environmentVariables.description: OTLP/HTTP collector URL; when set, every stored trace is also exported as OpenTelemetry spans (best-effort, asynchronous)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_DOMAINS
environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated domain allowlist for verify_citations fetches (only consulted when IRIS_CITATION_ALLOW_FETCH is on)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_TRANSPORT
environmentVariables.description: Transport: stdio (default) or http; same as --transport

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_HOST
environmentVariables.description: Bind host for the HTTP transport (default 127.0.0.1); only used with --transport http

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated Origin allowlist for the HTTP transport and dashboard CORS (default http://localhost:*)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD_HOST
environmentVariables.description: Bind host for the dashboard (default 127.0.0.1); same as --dashboard-host

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OTEL_HEADERS
environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated key=value headers sent with every OTLP export (for example an auth token for your collector)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
environmentVariables.description: service.name resource attribute on exported spans (default iris-eval)

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OTEL_TIMEOUT_MS
environmentVariables.description: Timeout in milliseconds for each OTLP export request

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_WEBHOOK_URL
environmentVariables.description: The receiver of the webhook that fires on a moment (docs/webhooks.md); merged over notify.webhook in config.json

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_WEBHOOK_SECRET
environmentVariables.description: The signing key of that webhook (any string, or whsec_ + base64); the iris format refuses to run without one

environmentVariables.description: Keep columns read from large files for fast follow-up questions: ask (default), on or off.

environmentVariables.description: Folder for saved large-file columns. Default: the system temp folder.

environmentVariables.description: Refuse data files larger than this (MB). Default: no limit.

environmentVariables.name: STATS_EXPLORER_APPROVAL_SECRET
environmentVariables.description: Orchestrated mode only: shared secret (32+ characters) the orchestrator signs decisions with.

environmentVariables.name: STATS_EXPLORER_AUDIT_LOG
environmentVariables.description: Path of a JSON Lines file recording every Jev checkpoint decision.

environmentVariables.name: GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

One of this token, GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE, GITLAB_JOB_TOKEN, GITLAB_AUTH_COOKIE_PATH, or GITLAB_USE_OAUTH=true must be set. Create a token with the GitLab scopes the tools need, such as api or read_api.

environmentVariables.name: GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE

environmentVariables.name: NOETIVE_EMBEDDINGS_URL
environmentVariables.description: An OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint you run. Set it and embeddings are computed on this machine rather than by Noetive: a publish carries the vector alongside its text, and a query's anchor phrases are replaced by vectors so they are never sent. This is not confidential publishing: message text still travels, because that is what a search returns. The endpoint must answer to the same model name as NOETIVE_MODEL and return NOETIVE_DIMENSIONS values. Plain http is accepted only for a loopback address. Inside a container 127.0.0.1 is the container itself; use host.docker.internal.
